title: The regulatory map
oneLiner: The SFO and the SFC form the base of Hong Kong securities regulation, and a bank meets them as a registered institution alongside the HKMA.
keyPoints: **Statute:** The Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) consolidated earlier securities and futures laws and commenced on 1 April 2003. It is the starting point for every question.
**Regulator:** The [[SFC]] continues under s.3 and has the regulatory objectives set out in s.4, including investor protection and reducing systemic risk.
**Layers:** The Ordinance sits above subsidiary legislation. Codes under s.399 are guidance, not subsidiary legislation, but a court must take their relevant provisions into account.
**Scope:** s.5(1)(b) gives the SFC supervision of recognized bodies and of other regulated persons, but of a registered institution only the activities the Ordinance requires it to regulate.
**Bank route:** A bank registers as a [[registered institution]] under s.119, and the HKMA supervises its securities business day to day.
**Counsel's role:** Read the statute first, then the rules and codes, and confirm each registered institution's status on the SFC register under s.136.

deepDive.heading: The SFC and its statute
deepDive.lede: The SFO is the framework, and the SFC is the body that administers it.
points: **Commencement:** The Ordinance consolidated earlier securities and futures laws and commenced on 1 April 2003.
**Continuity:** After the repeal of the Securities and Futures Commission Ordinance (Cap. 24), s.3 continues the Commission under its original name as a body corporate.
**Objectives:** s.4 sets six objectives, including investor protection, minimizing crime and misconduct, and reducing systemic risk.

**Board and funding:** Under Sch. 2, Pt 1, the Chief Executive appoints the chairman, the chief executive officer and the other members. The SFC says it is funded mainly by transaction levies and licensing fees.
**Anatomy:** The SFO has 20 main Parts (I to XVII, plus IIIA, IVA and XIVA) and 10 Schedules.
deepDive.takeaway: Start with the statute, then the Commission's functions and objectives, because each rule is read against them.

deepDive.heading: Layers of rules
deepDive.lede: Rules carry different legal force, and the Ordinance is the strongest layer.
points: **Statute:** The SFO sets the regulated activities, the licensing and registration regime, the offences and the disciplinary powers.
**Subsidiary legislation:** Made under the SFO, such as the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules (Cap. 571N) and the Securities and Futures (Client Money) Rules (Cap. 571I).
**Codes and guidelines:** Published under s.399. Failure to comply does not by itself lead to proceedings, but a code is admissible in evidence and any relevant provision must be taken into account.
**Circulars and FAQs:** These show how the regulators read their rules. They are useful but sit at the weakest layer.
deepDive.takeaway: Read statute first, then subsidiary legislation, then codes, then circulars and FAQs. A code can still shape how a supervisory matter is judged.

deepDive.heading: Market infrastructure and listing
deepDive.lede: Exchanges, clearing houses and listings have their own Parts and filing steps.
points: **Recognition:** Part III provides for recognition of exchange companies, clearing houses and exchange controllers, which the SFC supervises under s.5(1)(b).
**Listing filings:** Under Cap. 571V, s.5, a copy of a listing application must be filed with the SFC within one business day after it is submitted to a recognized exchange company.
**Objection power:** Under Cap. 571V, s.6, the SFC may require further information and may object to a listing.
**Exchange rules:** The exchange's own listing rules apply alongside Cap. 571V and must be checked separately.
deepDive.takeaway: For any listing work, build the SFC filing and the possibility of an objection into the timetable from the start.

deepDive.heading: Other bodies
deepDive.lede: Several bodies decide disputes, bring cases or pay compensation under the SFO.
points: **Takeovers:** Takeovers and share buy-back codes are published under s.399(2).
**Market Misconduct Tribunal:** Part XIII provides for this tribunal, which hears market misconduct cases.
**Securities and Futures Appeals Tribunal:** Part XI deals with appeals to this tribunal.
**Investor compensation:** Part XII provides for investor compensation.
**Courts and offences:** Criminal offences for dealings in securities and futures contracts are in Part XIV.
**Disclosure:** Part XIVA covers disclosure of inside information and Part XV covers disclosure of interests.
deepDive.takeaway: Know which forum decides each type of dispute before a problem arises.

deepDive.heading: Where a bank sits
deepDive.lede: A bank is an authorized institution, and its securities business is regulated as a registered institution.
points: **Registration:** A bank applies under s.119 to be registered for one or more regulated activities. The SFC refers the application to the Monetary Authority.
**Fitness advice:** The Monetary Authority advises whether the applicant is a fit and proper person, and the SFC must have regard to that advice (s.119(3) and (4)).
**Relevant individuals:** Individuals in regulated functions are recorded under Banking Ordinance s.20, and the Monetary Authority can take disciplinary action against them under s.58A.
**Executive officers:** Under Banking Ordinance s.71C, an executive officer needs the Monetary Authority's written consent.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat the HKMA as the daily counterpart, and the SFC as the authority that can still act on the registered institution's securities business.

deepDive.heading: Reading the rules as counsel
deepDive.lede: A fixed order keeps each conclusion tied to its source.
points: **Statute first:** Confirm the section in the SFO or the Banking Ordinance before relying on any summary.
**Then the rules:** Check subsidiary legislation, then the codes under s.399.
**Then the guidance:** Circulars, FAQs and HKMA material explain how the regulators apply the law, and they change over time.
**Check the register:** Use the SFC register under s.136 to confirm the status of any counterparty or entity.
deepDive.takeaway: Record which layer each conclusion rests on, so the advice can be updated when the guidance moves.

provisions.title: Securities and Futures Commission
provisions.summary: Continues the body established under the repealed Securities and Futures Commission Ordinance (Cap. 24) under its original name, as a body corporate able to sue and be sued. The Commission's receipts are not subject to tax under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and Sch. 2 governs its constitution and proceedings.
provisions.counselNote: Use the statutory name in correspondence, contracts and regulatory filings. Sch. 2 governs the board, which matters when the bank engages with the Commission at senior level.

provisions.title: Regulatory objectives of Commission
provisions.summary: Lists six objectives: fairness, efficiency, competitiveness, transparency and orderliness of the industry; public understanding of financial services; protection of investors; minimizing crime and misconduct; reducing systemic risk; and assisting the Financial Secretary with financial stability.
provisions.counselNote: These objectives frame how the SFC judges conduct, fitness and product design, so a bank's securities business is tested against them.

provisions.title: Functions and powers of Commission
provisions.summary: Sets the SFC's functions so far as reasonably practicable, including supervising recognized bodies and regulated persons. For registered institutions, the SFC regulates only the activities that the relevant provisions require it to regulate.
provisions.counselNote: This carve-out explains why the HKMA carries most day-to-day supervision of a bank's securities business, while the SFC keeps its statutory role for the activities the Ordinance reserves to it.

provisions.title: Registered institutions
provisions.summary: An authorized financial institution may apply to the SFC to be registered for one or more regulated activities, other than Type 3 and Type 8. The SFC refers the application to the Monetary Authority, which advises on fitness and properness, and the registration may be subject to reasonable conditions.
provisions.counselNote: Registration is per regulated activity, so the scope of the bank's securities business drives the application. Conditions can be changed by the SFC, so track them after registration.

provisions.title: Disciplinary action in respect of registered institutions, etc.
provisions.summary: Where a regulated person is guilty of misconduct, or the SFC is of the opinion that it is not fit and proper, the SFC may revoke or suspend a registered institution's registration in whole or in part, reprimand it publicly or privately, and prohibit specified steps. The power is subject to s.198. Separately, under s.196(2) the SFC may order a pecuniary penalty of up to the greater of $10 million or three times the profit gained or loss avoided.
provisions.counselNote: The SFC keeps this disciplinary power over a registered institution's securities activities even though the HKMA supervises day to day. Treat it as a live exposure in the risk register.

provisions.title: Codes or guidelines by Commission
provisions.summary: The SFC may publish codes and guidelines, including codes on takeovers and share buy-backs. A failure to comply does not by itself lead to proceedings, but a code is admissible in evidence and any relevant provision must be taken into account. Codes are not subsidiary legislation, and the SFC must consult the Monetary Authority on codes that apply to authorized institutions as registered institutions.
provisions.counselNote: Codes are not hard law, but they are the yardstick a court or regulator uses to judge conduct. Map every code that applies to the bank's securities business and treat its requirements as controls.

provisions.title: Commission to maintain register of licensed persons and registered institutions
provisions.summary: The SFC must maintain a register of licensed persons and registered institutions, recording conditions, executive officers and, for licensed representatives, their principals. The register is designed so that members of the public can check whether they are dealing with a licensed person or registered institution.
provisions.counselNote: Check the register before onboarding a counterparty, intermediary or distributor. Do not rely only on internal records of the bank's own registration status and conditions.

provisions.title: Regulated Activities
provisions.summary: Sets out the activities that are regulated activities under the Ordinance, grouped into numbered types. Whether a particular product or service is caught depends on the type and on the definitions that apply to it.
provisions.counselNote: Map each product and service to a regulated activity type before launch. The mapping decides whether registration is needed for that activity.

provisions.instrument: Securities and Futures (Stock Market Listing) Rules (Cap. 571V)
provisions.title: Powers of the Commission to require further information and to object to listing
provisions.summary: Under s.5, a copy of a listing application must be filed with the SFC within one business day after it is submitted to a recognized exchange company. Under s.6, the SFC may require further information within 10 business days, and may object to a listing within 10 business days, with reasons, if the application is non-compliant, false or misleading, or the listing is not in the interest of the investing public or the public interest.
provisions.counselNote: Where the bank is involved in a listing, the filing and the SFC's objection power must be built into the timetable. Confirm the exchange's own requirements alongside these rules.

provisions.title: Register of authorized institutions, etc.
provisions.summary: The Monetary Authority must keep a register of authorized institutions and related persons. For registered institutions, the register includes each relevant individual and the capacity in which that individual performs a regulated function. Relevant individuals are defined in s.20(10).
provisions.counselNote: Staff in securities roles at the bank are relevant individuals. Keep the bank's submissions on them accurate and current, because they feed the HKMA's register.

provisions.title: Executive officers of registered institutions require Monetary Authority’s consent
provisions.summary: No person may become or act as an executive officer of a registered institution without the Monetary Authority's written consent. The Monetary Authority must refuse consent unless satisfied that the person is fit and proper, and consent may be withdrawn.
provisions.counselNote: Executive officer consent is a precondition, so build it into onboarding and internal transfers. Acting before consent is an offence, not merely a process error.

provisions.instrument: SFC and HKMA Memorandum of Understanding on securities activities of authorized institutions
provisions.title: Division of supervision for registered institutions
provisions.summary: Records the shared responsibility of the HKMA and the SFC for registered institutions and their relevant individuals. The HKMA remains the front-line supervisor of registered institutions, and the SFC regulates the securities activities they carry on.
provisions.counselNote: The MoU sets the working relationship between the two regulators. Read its text, published by the HKMA, before relying on any specific allocation of responsibility.

checklist: **Confirm registration status:** Check the bank's registration conditions under s.119 and the SFC register under s.136.
**Map every product to a regulated activity:** Record each product and service against Sch. 5 before launch.
**Document the SFC and HKMA split:** Keep a note of which regulator covers which obligation for each regulated activity.
**Register the codes:** Maintain a list of the s.399 codes that apply to the securities business, and map each requirement to a control.
**Track executive officers and relevant individuals:** Keep current the consents under Banking Ordinance s.71C and the entries under s.20.
**Build the listing filing into timetables:** Where the bank is involved in a listing, add the Cap. 571V copy filing and the SFC's objection window to the plan.
**Use a statute-first reading order:** Record the section relied on for each conclusion, and the layer it sits in.
**Raise boundary questions early:** When a product sits between SFC and HKMA responsibility, ask both regulators before launch.
itAngle: **Activity inventory:** Keep a product-to-regulated-activity inventory as a governed data set, so the registration scope can be checked against it.
**Register data:** Store the bank's relevant individual and executive officer data in a form that can be reconciled to the HKMA and SFC records.
**Register checks in onboarding:** Automate checks of counterparties and intermediaries against the SFC register, and log each result.
**Filing workflows:** Track listing copy filings and any SFC requests as workflow items with owners and deadlines.
bankNotes: **Registration:** A bank conducting securities business does so as a registered institution under s.119, registered for each regulated activity, rather than as a licensed corporation.
**Dual supervision:** The HKMA supervises day to day, while the SFC keeps its functions under s.5 and its disciplinary powers under s.196.
**Relevant individuals:** Staff in regulated functions are recorded under Banking Ordinance s.20, and executive officers need consent under s.71C.
**Shared oversight:** Under the MoU, the HKMA and the SFC share responsibility for registered institutions, so a matter raised with one regulator may reach the other.
pitfalls: **Assuming HKMA means no SFC:** Securities activities of a registered institution remain subject to SFC codes and to the powers in s.196.
**Treating codes as optional:** A breach of a code is not by itself actionable, but a court must take its relevant provisions into account.
**Starting before registration:** Beginning a regulated activity before registration for it.
**Relying on internal records:** Treating the bank's own file on its registration status as sufficient, rather than checking the public register under s.136.

glossary.definition: The Securities and Futures Commission, the regulator of the securities and futures industry under the Securities and Futures Ordinance. It is independent of government and funded mainly by transaction levies and licensing fees.
Cap. 571, the core statute for securities and futures business in Hong Kong. It consolidated earlier laws and commenced on 1 April 2003.
An authorized financial institution registered by the SFC under s.119 for one or more regulated activities. The HKMA supervises its securities business day to day.
A corporation licensed by the SFC under Part V to carry on regulated activities. It is the licensing route for non-bank intermediaries.
An activity listed in Sch. 5 to the Ordinance, such as dealing in securities or advising on securities. Carrying one on in Hong Kong generally requires a licence or registration for it.
An individual engaged in a regulated function at a registered institution, recorded under Banking Ordinance s.20 and subject to disciplinary action by the Monetary Authority under s.58A.
A code or guideline the SFC publishes under s.399. It is not subsidiary legislation, its breach is not by itself actionable, and it is admissible in evidence in proceedings.
A listing step under Cap. 571V in which a copy of the listing application is also filed with the SFC, which may then require information or object to the listing.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, which acts through the Monetary Authority under the Banking Ordinance. It is the frontline supervisor of registered institutions' securities business.
An exchange company recognized under Part III of the Ordinance to operate a market in Hong Kong. The SFC supervises such companies under s.5.

title: Regulated activities & the perimeter
oneLiner: The SFO perimeter turns on whether a business in one of 13 regulated activities is carried on, so product classification comes first.
keyPoints: **Prohibition:** s.114(1) bars anyone from carrying on a business in a [[regulated activity]], or holding out as doing so, unless licensed, registered or exempt.
**Regulated functions:** s.114(3) separately bars performing a [[regulated function]] in relation to a regulated activity carried on as a business, unless an exemption applies.

**Thirteen types:** Sch. 5, Pt 1 lists 13 regulated activities. Types 11 and 12 (OTC derivatives) belong to a regime not yet fully in force, so check their commencement notes on HKeL, and Type 13 has been in force since 2 October 2024.
**Definitions first:** whether a product is a security, a futures contract or a [[structured product]] (Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.1A) decides the question before any licence analysis begins.
**Cross-border:** s.115 treats active marketing to the Hong Kong public from abroad as carrying on the business in Hong Kong, so group marketing is within reach.
**Bank position:** an authorized institution is registered under s.119 for the activities it carries on, not licensed as a corporation, and its individuals must be entered on the MA's register.

conceptMap.caption: The perimeter test in order. A yes at the final step means the s.114(1) prohibition applies unless an exemption is available.

deepDive.heading: The prohibition and its two limbs
deepDive.lede: Section 114 restricts two different things, and the penalties for each are separate.
points: **Business limb:** s.114(1)(a) bars carrying on a business in a [[regulated activity]], and s.114(1)(b) bars holding out as doing so.
**Function limb:** s.114(3) bars performing a [[regulated function]] in relation to a regulated activity carried on as a business, and holding out as performing one.

**Exemptions:** s.114(2) exempts a [[licensed corporation]] for the activity it is licensed for, and an authorized institution registered under s.119 for the activity it is registered for. Under s.114(4), a [[licensed representative]] and an individual entered on the MA's register under s.20 of the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155) may perform functions.
**'As a business':** Whether an activity is carried on as a business is a question of fact, usually decided by its regularity, scale and commercial character.

**Penalties:** on indictment, a breach of s.114(1) without reasonable excuse carries a fine of HK$5 million and 7 years' imprisonment, plus HK$100,000 a day for a continuing offence (s.114(8)(a)). A breach of s.114(3) carries HK$1 million and 2 years (s.114(9)(a)).
deepDive.takeaway: The business and function limbs carry separate exposure, so an unlicensed product and an unregistered individual are two distinct risks.

deepDive.heading: The 13 regulated activities
deepDive.lede: Schedule 5, Part 1 lists the activities. The grouping below is for orientation only.
points: **Dealing and financing:** Type 1 (dealing in securities), Type 2 (dealing in futures contracts), Type 3 (leveraged foreign exchange trading) and Type 8 (securities margin financing).
**Advising:** Type 4 (advising on securities), Type 5 (advising on futures contracts) and Type 6 (advising on corporate finance).
**Managing and rating:** Type 9 (asset management) and Type 10 (providing credit rating services).

**Infrastructure:** Type 7 (providing automated trading services), and Types 11 to 13 (OTC derivatives dealing and advice, client clearing for OTC derivatives, and depositary services for relevant CISs).

**Commencement:** Types 11 and 12 belong to the OTC derivatives regime, which is not yet fully in force; check the commencement notes on HKeL before relying on either. Type 13 (depositary services for relevant CISs) has been in force since 2 October 2024.
deepDive.takeaway: Match every product and service the bank offers to one or more types, and record the match in the product file.

deepDive.heading: Definitions that decide the question
deepDive.lede: Before the activity test, the product must be a security, a futures contract or another defined instrument.
points: **Securities:** Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.1 defines the term widely. It covers shares, debentures, rights and interests in them, and interests in collective investment schemes, among others. It excludes, for example, shares or debentures of a private company under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622, s.11) and MPF or ORSO scheme interests. Read the full definition against the product terms.

**Structured products:** Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.1A treats an instrument as a [[structured product]] where some or all of its return, amount due or settlement method is determined by reference to specified factors, subject to exclusions.
**OTC derivatives:** the OTC types in Sch. 5 (Types 11 and 12) cover OTC derivative products, which the Ordinance defines. Read the definition before scoping a product against those types.

**Tokens:** many crypto-assets fall outside the SFO definition of securities, but a token that meets the definition is a security and within the regime. Classify each token by its rights, not its label.
deepDive.takeaway: Classification is a product decision with legal consequences, so the conclusion belongs in the product approval file.

deepDive.heading: Exclusions and the edges of each type
deepDive.lede: Each type's definition carves out certain acts, so an activity can be in scope for one type and excluded for another.
points: **Where to look:** Sch. 5, Pt 2 sets out the excluded services and carve-outs for each type. Read the paragraph for the exact type before relying on it.
**Intermediaries and group members:** an exclusion may depend on who performs the act and under what arrangement. Check the conditions, not just the label.

**Leveraged FX:** Type 3 cannot be registered under s.119(1), so an authorized institution does not take Type 3 registration. Nor does it need to: para (xii) of the definition of leveraged foreign exchange trading in Sch. 5, Pt 2 excludes transactions by an authorized financial institution.
**Recording reliance:** for each exclusion relied on, record the paragraph, the facts that meet its conditions and the date of review.
deepDive.takeaway: An exclusion is only as good as the facts that meet its conditions, so document those facts when the product is approved.

deepDive.heading: Reaching into Hong Kong (s.115)
deepDive.lede: Conduct outside Hong Kong is caught when it actively targets the Hong Kong public.
points: **Trigger:** s.115(1)(a) applies where a person actively markets to the public any services it provides, from inside or outside Hong Kong, by itself or through someone on its behalf.

**Test:** s.115(1)(b) asks whether those services, if provided in Hong Kong, would be a regulated activity. If so, the offshore provision is treated as carrying on that activity in Hong Kong (s.115(1)(i)).
**Holding out and functions:** the marketing is treated as holding out (s.115(1)(ii)), and s.115(2) applies the same approach to regulated functions marketed to the public.
**Actively markets:** the phrase is the trigger. Whether a given campaign counts is a fact-specific question, to be assessed with reference to SFC guidance.
**Offers to the public:** s.103 separately restricts certain advertisements and invitations about investments. It is covered in the offers stage and is flagged here only as a boundary.

deepDive.heading: Neighbouring regimes
deepDive.lede: Several other regimes sit beside the SFO, and some overlap with it.
points: **Virtual assets:** Part 5B of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO, Cap. 615) licenses [[virtual asset trading platforms|virtual asset trading platform]] for non-security tokens, from 1 June 2023. Section 53ZRB defines when a person provides a VA service, and s.53ZRD requires a licence to carry on that business.

**Dual status:** a token that is a security falls under the SFO. A platform dealing in both kinds of token may need licences under both ordinances. Confirm the SFC's current position before relying on a single-licence route.
**Stablecoins:** the Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) commenced on 1 August 2025 and is administered by the HKMA, outside the SFO. Check the status of any licence a product relies on.

**Other regimes:** insurance (Insurance Ordinance, Cap. 41), money lending (Money Lenders Ordinance, Cap. 163) and stored value facilities (Payment Systems and Stored Value Facilities Ordinance, Cap. 584, under the HKMA) have their own regimes outside this stage.
**Bank position:** an authorized institution is registered under s.119 for the regulated activities it carries on, rather than licensed as a corporation (s.114(2)(b)).
deepDive.takeaway: Map each product against all of these regimes, not just the SFO, before choosing the licence or registration route.

provisions.title: Restriction on carrying on business in regulated activities, etc.
provisions.summary: Bars any person from carrying on a business in a regulated activity, or holding out as doing so, subject to exemptions for licensed corporations, registered authorized institutions and persons authorized under s.95(2). A breach without reasonable excuse is an offence, with a fine of HK$5 million and 7 years' imprisonment on indictment.
provisions.counselNote: This is the core prohibition on product launches and marketing. Check each new product against the exemptions, and note that a continuing offence adds HK$100,000 a day on indictment.

provisions.title: Restriction on carrying on business in regulated activities, etc.
provisions.summary: Bars performing a regulated function in relation to a regulated activity carried on as a business, or holding out as doing so. Exempt are licensed representatives acting for their principal, and individuals entered on the MA's register under s.20 of the Banking Ordinance for a registered institution. A breach on indictment carries HK$1 million and 2 years.
provisions.counselNote: For the bank, staff performing securities functions must be on the register under s.20 of the Banking Ordinance, or they fall outside the exemption. Check this at hiring and on any change of role.

provisions.title: Application of section 114 in relation to conduct or activities outside Hong Kong
provisions.summary: Treats a person who actively markets to the public services that would be a regulated activity if provided in Hong Kong as carrying on that business. This applies whether the marketing is in Hong Kong or from abroad, and the same approach covers regulated functions marketed to the public.
provisions.counselNote: Offshore group marketing into Hong Kong brings the offshore business within the prohibition. Review overseas campaigns, referral programmes and group launches before they reach Hong Kong users.

provisions.title: Corporations to be licensed for carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: Empowers the Commission to grant a corporation a licence for one or more regulated activities; the requirement to hold one derives from the s.114(1) prohibition. Section 114(2)(a) cross-refers to ss.116 and 117 for licensed corporations.
provisions.counselNote: This is the licensed corporation route used by group companies and fintech partners that are not banks. The bank itself uses registration under s.119.

provisions.title: Offence to issue advertisements, invitations or documents relating to investments in certain cases
provisions.summary: Creates an offence for issuing advertisements, invitations or documents about investments in specified circumstances. It is covered in the offers stage and is cited here only to mark the boundary with s.115.
provisions.counselNote: Offer and marketing material for investment products carries a separate offence risk from the business prohibition. Route such material through legal review.

provisions.title: Regulated Activities
provisions.summary: Lists the 13 regulated activities in Part 1, with the definitions and exclusions for each in Part 2. Types 11 and 12 belong to the OTC derivatives regime, which is not yet fully in force, and Type 13 has been in force since 2 October 2024.
provisions.counselNote: Each product should map to one or more types, and each exclusion relied on should be recorded against its paragraph. Types 11 and 12 belong to the OTC derivatives regime, which is not yet fully in force.

provisions.title: Meaning of structured product
provisions.summary: Defines a structured product as an instrument whose return, amount due or settlement method is determined by reference to specified factors, subject to exclusions. The definitions of securities and futures contracts sit in s.1 of the same Part.
provisions.counselNote: Classification decides the perimeter. Read each definition against the product's terms, test packaged and derivative-linked products against s.1A, and record the conclusion before launch.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Meaning of providing VA service and performing regulated function
provisions.summary: Treats a person who actively markets to the public, from inside or outside Hong Kong, virtual asset services that the person provides as providing those services in Hong Kong. Section 53ZRB also defines when a person provides a VA service.
provisions.counselNote: This is the virtual asset counterpart of s.115. Offshore marketing of crypto products to Hong Kong users raises a licensing question under this regime too.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Licence required for carrying on VA service business
provisions.summary: Prohibits a person from carrying on a business of providing a VA service, or holding out as doing so, unless licensed. It also bars performing a regulated function for such a business. A breach without reasonable excuse is an offence, with a fine of HK$5 million and 7 years' imprisonment on indictment, plus HK$100,000 a day for a continuing offence.
provisions.counselNote: This applies to the bank only if it or a group entity offers virtual asset trading in Hong Kong. Coordinate with the virtual assets stage before any such product.

provisions.title: Registered institutions
provisions.summary: Allows the SFC, on application by an authorized financial institution, to register it for one or more regulated activities, other than Type 3 and Type 8. Registration cannot cover those two types.
provisions.counselNote: The bank does not need Type 3 status for its own FX business, because the leveraged FX definition in Sch. 5, Pt 2 excludes transactions by an authorized financial institution (para (xii)). Group companies that are not authorized institutions get no such exclusion.

checklist: **Map each product and feature** to one or more Sch. 5 types in a written memo, and keep the memo with the product file.
**Confirm the RI registration** covers every type actually carried on, and check Types 3 and 8 specifically before relying on any registration.
**Classify each structured product and token** against Sch. 1 and s.1A, and record the reasoning.
**Maintain the register** of individuals under s.114(4)(b) and the Banking Ordinance s.20, linked to onboarding and role changes.
**Screen offshore group marketing** against s.115 before any campaign reaches Hong Kong users.
**Keep an exclusions log** under Sch. 5, Pt 2, with the paragraph relied on, the facts that meet it and the review date.
**Track commencement** of Types 11 and 12 and of any new type, and update the perimeter map when status changes.
**Route virtual asset products** through the AMLO Part 5B analysis alongside the SFO perimeter review.
itAngle: **Geo-targeting controls:** Tag marketing assets and campaign audiences by target market, so that a s.115 review can see what reached Hong Kong users. Geo-blocking is a supporting control, not a complete answer.
**Product inventory:** Keep a machine-readable inventory of products and features with their Sch. 5 mapping. New features that change a product's rights can change its classification.
**Register data:** The register of individuals under s.114(4)(b) ties to HR and access provisioning. Automate onboarding and offboarding so the MA register stays accurate.
**Exclusion evidence:** Exclusions depend on facts such as who performs an act and through which channel. Log those facts in the systems that carry out the activity, so the evidence is retrievable.
bankNotes: **Registration scope:** The bank's securities activities are bounded by its registration under s.119. Section 119(1) excludes Types 3 and 8 from registration, so check the register entry for every other type the bank carries on.

**Staff register:** Individuals performing securities functions must be entered on the MA's register under s.20 of the Banking Ordinance (s.114(4)(b)). Without that entry, the exemption does not apply to them.
**Group companies:** Affiliates that carry on regulated activities need their own licence or registration. The bank's registration does not extend to them (s.114(2)).
**Marketing into Hong Kong:** Overseas group entities that actively market to the Hong Kong public fall within s.115. Set a pre-launch perimeter check for any cross-border campaign.
pitfalls: **Equating the bank with the product:** Assuming that a bank product is outside the perimeter because it is a bank product. Registration covers only the activities registered.
**Overlooking group marketing:** Assuming that an offshore affiliate's campaign is not the bank's concern, when s.115 can bring it within the prohibition.
**Assuming a token is outside the SFO:** Treating every crypto-asset as outside the definitions without checking whether its rights make it a security.
**Assuming staff are covered:** Believing that the bank's registration covers every employee. Only individuals entered on the register under s.114(4)(b) are within the exemption.

glossary.definition: One of the 13 activities listed in Sch. 5, Pt 1. Carrying on a business in one without a licence, registration or exemption breaches s.114(1).
A function such as dealing, advising or managing, performed in relation to a regulated activity. Performing one as a business without the right licence or register entry breaches s.114(3).
A corporation licensed under s.116 or s.117 for specified regulated activities. Its licence covers only the activities named in it.
An authorized institution registered under s.119 for specified regulated activities. Its registration sets the boundary of its securities business.
An individual licensed to act for a principal, usually a licensed corporation, in a regulated activity for which the representative is licensed.
An instrument whose return, amount due or settlement method depends on reference factors set out in Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.1A. Packaged and derivative-linked products often fall within it.
An arrangement in which participants pool money for profit or income, with the operation managed by others. Interests in one are securities under Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.1.
Presenting oneself, through marketing or conduct, as carrying on a regulated activity or performing a regulated function. Section 114 catches this even without actual business.
Promoting services to the public, by oneself or through another, from inside or outside Hong Kong. It is the trigger in s.115 and is decided on the facts.
A platform trading virtual assets that are not securities. It is licensed under Part 5B of the AMLO and is subject to the SFC's requirements for such platforms.

title: Licensing & registration
oneLiner: A bank that deals in securities usually registers under s.119 on HKMA advice, rather than applying for a licence under s.116.
keyPoints: **Two routes:** A licensed corporation applies under s.116. An authorized institution applies to become a [[registered institution]] under s.119. The routes differ in who advises and which capital rules apply.
**Fit and proper:** The regulator weighs financial standing, competence, conduct and reputation, for the firm and its key people, before granting either status (s.129).
**RI decisions:** The SFC refers every RI application to the HKMA, which advises on fitness, and the SFC may rely wholly on that advice (s.119(2)–(4)).
**Ownership and premises:** Substantial shareholders need prior SFC approval (ss.131, 132), and premises used for securities records need approval (s.130).
**Continuing duties:** Changes in information are notified within 7 business days, cessation is notified in advance, and annual fees fall due within a month of each anniversary (s.135; s.138).
**Counsel's role:** Map the application, the individuals who need approval and the notice calendar before the bank starts any regulated activity.

deepDive.lede: An authorized institution would ordinarily take the registration route under s.119 rather than the licensing route under s.116.

visual.caption: Same activities, different gatekeeper. Check the capital and approval details for the bank's own structure.

points: **Licensed corporation:** Under s.116 the SFC grants a licence for one or more regulated activities to a company or qualifying foreign corporation, and applications to approve its responsible officers must have been lodged (s.116(2)(b)).
**Temporary licences:** Under s.117 an overseas corporation may get a temporary licence for up to 3 months, for activities other than Types 3, 7, 8 and 9.
**Registered institution:** Under s.119 an authorized institution applies to the SFC for registration. The SFC must refer the application to the HKMA.
**Scope limit:** An RI registration cannot cover Type 3 or Type 8 regulated activities, which are excluded from the s.119 route.
**Individuals:** Licensed representatives are licensed under s.120 for licensed corporations, while an RI's executive officers need the MA's consent under the Banking Ordinance.

deepDive.heading: Fit and proper test
deepDive.lede: Both routes turn on the same statutory test, applied to the firm and to the people who run it.
points: **The test:** The SFC or the MA must have regard to financial status or solvency, relevant qualifications and experience, the ability to act competently, honestly and fairly, and reputation, character, reliability and financial integrity (s.129(1)(a)–(d)).

**Who is tested:** For a corporation, the firm and its officers. For an authorized institution, the institution and its directors, chief executive, managers and executive officers (s.129(1)(i)–(iii)).
**Guidelines:** The Fit and Proper Guidelines are issued by the SFC and are not law, but they show how the SFC reads s.129. Use the version current on the SFC website.

**Competence:** The Guidelines on Competence set qualification and experience standards for representatives, responsible officers, and RI executive officers and relevant individuals. Check the current version before relying on it.
**After grant:** Fitness is not a one-off test. Officer changes can change the firm's standing, so treat them as regulatory events.
deepDive.takeaway: Test each proposed officer against s.129 before the regulator asks.

deepDive.heading: Applying as a registered institution
deepDive.lede: The RI application is filed with the SFC but depends on the HKMA's view.

visual.caption: The SFC makes the decision, but the HKMA's advice feeds into it.

items.label: Submit application to SFC
items.note: Prescribed form, fee and supporting documents

points: **Filing:** Applications are made to the SFC in the prescribed manner and on payment of the prescribed fee (s.119(1)). The Licensing Handbook describes the process, and online filing runs through the SFC's WINGS online platform.
**Referral:** The SFC must refer an RI application to the HKMA. The HKMA considers it, consults the SFC and advises whether the applicant is fit and proper (s.119(2)–(3)).
**Reliance:** The SFC must have regard to that advice and may rely on it wholly or partly (s.119(4)).
**Conditions:** Registration is subject to reasonable conditions, which the SFC may amend or add to by notice (s.119(5)).
deepDive.takeaway: Agree the activity scope and the HKMA timetable before filing.

deepDive.heading: Owners, approvals and premises
deepDive.lede: Ownership and premises changes need approval before they take effect.
points: **Substantial shareholder:** Under Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.6, a person, alone or with associates, is a substantial shareholder if it has an interest in more than 10% of the issued shares or voting power, or controls 35% or more of the voting power of a corporation that can itself control more than 10% of the corporation concerned (indirect control).
**Approval:** Becoming or continuing as a substantial shareholder of a licensed corporation needs prior SFC approval (s.131(1)). The SFC refuses unless the firm remains fit and proper (s.132(1)–(2)).
**Conditions:** Shareholder approvals carry conditions that the SFC can amend or revoke by notice (s.132(3)–(4)).
**Premises:** A licensed corporation may keep its records at premises only with the SFC's prior written approval (s.130(3)).

**Bank point:** Section 132 is framed around licensed corporations. For an RI, the Banking Ordinance regulates the controllers of an authorized institution (Cap. 155, s.2), so check those approvals there, and check group LC subsidiaries separately.
deepDive.takeaway: Keep a shareholding register and an approval calendar before any transfer completes.

deepDive.heading: Staying licensed or registered
deepDive.lede: Grant is the start of continuing duties, most of them with short deadlines.

items.label: Cessation
items.note: Notice before stopping a regulated activity (s.135(1))

items.label: Change of information
items.note: Notice after the change (s.135(3); Cap. 571S, s.4)

items.label: Annual fee
items.note: Due within a month after each anniversary (s.138(2))

items.label: Late payment
items.note: Monthly surcharge on the unpaid fee (s.138(3))

points: **Notices:** Cessation needs notice as soon as reasonably practicable and at least 7 business days before, and changes in information need notice within 7 business days (s.135(1), (3)).
**Address changes:** Seven business days' advance notice is needed for a new address for the regulated activity (s.135(2)).
**Prescribed information:** Cap. 571S sets out which changes must be notified and to whom, through the rule on changes and Schedule 3 (s.4).
**Financial Resources Rules:** Licensed corporations must keep financial resources and paid-up share capital at the levels in Cap. 571N, the amounts for each activity sit in its Schedule 1 table.
**Public register:** The SFC keeps a register of licensed persons and RIs, including conditions and executive officers (s.136(2)).
deepDive.takeaway: Set one compliance calendar covering notices, fees and returns.

deepDive.heading: The RI path in practice
deepDive.lede: For a bank, the route runs through the HKMA as well as the SFC.
points: **Authorized status first:** Only an authorized financial institution can apply for registration under s.119.
**Executive officers:** No person may act as an RI's executive officer without the MA's written consent, which the MA may withdraw (Banking Ordinance, Cap. 155, s.71C(1)).
**Relevant individuals:** Individuals who carry out regulated functions must meet the competence standards, so map them early against the Guidelines on Competence.
**HKMA role:** Under s.119(3) the HKMA advises the SFC on fitness, and it supervises the bank as an authorized institution under the Banking Ordinance.
**Capital:** The Financial Resources Rules govern licensed corporations under Cap. 571N, s.4. For an RI, check the Banking Ordinance capital regime rather than assuming the Rules apply.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat the HKMA and the SFC as joint approvers, and map both approvals in one schedule.

provisions.title: Corporations to be licensed for carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: The SFC may license a corporation on application and payment of the prescribed fee to carry on one or more regulated activities. The SFC must refuse unless the applicant is a company or a qualifying non-Hong Kong corporation, and responsible officer applications have been lodged.
provisions.counselNote: This is the route for a bank's non-bank subsidiary that does securities business. A bank itself registers under s.119 instead.

provisions.title: Grant of temporary licences to corporations for carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: The SFC may grant a temporary licence for up to 3 months, excluding Type 3, 7, 8 and 9 activities, to a corporation that conducts an equivalent business principally outside Hong Kong and meets the listed conditions.
provisions.counselNote: Relevant only where an overseas group entity starts Hong Kong securities business before a full licence is granted. Do not assume the temporary route is available for a bank's core activities.

provisions.title: Registered institutions
provisions.summary: An authorized financial institution may apply to the SFC to be registered for one or more regulated activities, other than Type 3 and Type 8. The SFC refers the application to the MA, which advises on fitness. The SFC must have regard to that advice and may rely on it, and registration is subject to reasonable conditions.
provisions.counselNote: This is the bank's route. Build the HKMA's referral step into the timetable, and treat the scope of activities as a condition that the bank must stay within.

provisions.title: Determination of fit and proper
provisions.summary: The SFC or the MA must consider financial status, qualifications and experience, the ability to act competently, honestly and fairly, and reputation and financial integrity. For an authorized institution the test covers the institution and its directors, chief executive, managers and executive officers.
provisions.counselNote: Use this list as the checklist for every officer and individual proposed for approval. Gaps found here usually cause delay, so run the review before filing.

provisions.title: Approval to become or continue to be substantial shareholder
provisions.summary: Under s.131(1) a person must not become or continue as a substantial shareholder of a licensed corporation without the SFC's prior approval under this section. The SFC refuses unless the corporation will remain fit and proper, and it may attach conditions that it can later amend or revoke by notice.
provisions.counselNote: The section applies to licensed corporations. For a bank's shareholding and group LC subsidiaries, confirm the regime that applies in each case.

provisions.title: References to substantial shareholder
provisions.summary: A person, alone or with associates, is a substantial shareholder of a corporation if it has an interest in more than 10% of the issued shares or voting power, or holds shares in another corporation giving it 35% or more of that corporation's voting power, where that corporation or a further one can control more than 10% of the corporation concerned (indirect control).
provisions.counselNote: Track holdings against the threshold by aggregating interests with associates, because the test is not limited to a single holder's direct interest.

provisions.title: Events to be reported by licensed persons and registered institutions
provisions.summary: A licensed person or RI that intends to stop a regulated activity must notify the SFC, and the MA for an RI, at least 7 business days beforehand. An intermediary must give 7 business days' advance notice of a change of address. Changes to information provided under Part V must be notified within 7 business days of the change, to the SFC and the MA where the information concerns an RI.
provisions.counselNote: These deadlines are short and easy to miss. Build them into the compliance calendar and assign an owner for each notice.

provisions.title: Annual fee and return
provisions.summary: A licensed person or RI must pay an annual fee set by rules, within one month after each anniversary of the grant unless the SFC approves another date. Late payment attracts a surcharge of 10% for the first month and 20% for each later month.
provisions.counselNote: Surcharges add up quickly, because each month adds 10% or 20% of the unpaid fee rather than compounding. Diarise each anniversary and confirm the fee amount under the fees rules before each payment.

provisions.instrument: Securities and Futures (Licensing and Registration) (Information) Rules (Cap. 571S)
provisions.title: Changes to be notified by intermediaries, licensed representatives and substantial shareholders
provisions.summary: Changes to information listed in Schedule 3 that was provided under Part V must be notified in writing, with a full description, within 7 business days after the change. The notice goes to the SFC and, for an RI, to the MA.
provisions.counselNote: Map each item in Schedule 3 to a data owner and a notice step. Rule-level changes are easy to overlook because they sit outside the Ordinance.

provisions.title: Paid-up share capital requirement for licensed corporations
provisions.summary: A licensed corporation must at all times maintain the financial resources required by the Rules (s.4). Section 5 sets a minimum paid-up share capital that depends on the regulated activities it is licensed for, with the amounts in a table in Schedule 1.
provisions.counselNote: These Rules apply to licensed corporations. They are not the capital test for an RI, so do not carry the figures into the bank's capital plan without checking.

provisions.title: Executive officers of registered institutions require Monetary Authority's consent
provisions.summary: No person may become or act as an executive officer of a registered institution without the MA's written consent, and the MA may attach conditions to that consent. The MA can withdraw the consent under the section.
provisions.counselNote: The bank must obtain MA consent for each executive officer, in addition to the SFC's fitness review. Map both approvals before appointing anyone.

provisions.title: Fit and Proper Guidelines
provisions.summary: The SFC's guidelines explain how it assesses the fitness of corporations and authorized institutions, and of their individuals, under Part V. They are issued by the SFC and do not have the force of law.
provisions.counselNote: Read the guidelines alongside the Ordinance when preparing officer submissions, using the version current on the SFC website.

checklist: **Confirm the route:** Record that the bank applies as an authorized institution under s.119, and list any group entity that needs a licence under s.116.
**Scope the activities:** List each regulated activity the bank will carry on, and confirm none is a Type 3 or Type 8 activity that falls outside the RI route.
**Build the officer map:** For each proposed director, chief executive, manager and executive officer, run the s.129 test and obtain the MA consent under s.71C.
**Map shareholders:** Track holdings against the Schedule 1 definition, aggregating associates, and diarise the s.132 approval for any new substantial shareholder.
**Plan premises:** Confirm where records will be kept, and check whether s.130 approval applies to any licensed corporation in the group.
**Set a notice calendar:** Diary the 7-business-day deadlines under s.135 and the annual fee under s.138 with named owners.
**Track prescribed changes:** Map each item in Schedule 3 to Cap. 571S, s.4 to an owner and a notice step.
**Check current versions:** Confirm the Fit and Proper Guidelines and the Guidelines on Competence on the SFC site before relying on them.
itAngle: **Officer records:** Officer and approval data feeds notices and the public register. Keep one authoritative record with dates, consents and conditions.
**Notice workflow:** Notices and fee payments need a workflow with deadlines, approvers and evidence of delivery, so that missed dates are visible in time.
**Records location:** For a licensed corporation, premises used to keep records need s.130 approval. Check how that applies to electronic storage and hosting outside Hong Kong.
**Evidence retrieval:** Keep approvals, conditions and notices quickly retrievable, because the SFC and HKMA will ask for them during an examination.
bankNotes: **Registration first:** The bank should register under s.119 for its securities activities, rather than seek an LC licence, unless a group company is the proper business vehicle.
**Capital route:** Capital for RI activities is set under the Banking Ordinance, not the Financial Resources Rules. Confirm that before building the capital plan.
**Group LCs:** Group companies that hold LC licences go through s.116 and s.132 separately, so keep their approvals in the group map.
**Two sign-offs:** An officer may need the HKMA's consent under s.71C and the SFC's fitness review, so start both processes early and in parallel.
pitfalls: **Missed notices:** Letting a 7-business-day deadline under s.135 pass during a busy period, which is a breach that is easy to overlook.
**Silent officer changes:** Appointing an officer without checking the s.129 test and the MA's consent under s.71C first.
**Wrong capital regime:** Applying the Financial Resources Rules figures to an RI without checking that the Rules govern it.
**Late fees:** Missing the annual fee window, which triggers escalating surcharges under s.138(3).

glossary.definition: A corporation licensed under s.116 to carry on one or more regulated activities. It is supervised by the SFC and is not a bank.
An authorized financial institution registered by the SFC under s.119 for specified regulated activities. The HKMA advises the SFC on fitness.
A bank or other institution authorized under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). It is the usual applicant for registration under s.119.

A person who, alone or with associates, has an interest in more than 10% of the issued shares or voting power of a corporation, including indirect control (Sch. 1, Pt 1, s.6). Becoming one of a licensed corporation needs prior SFC approval under s.132.
For an RI, an executive officer as defined in the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). The MA must consent in writing under s.71C before the individual acts in that role.
An individual approved by the SFC under s.126(1) as a responsible officer of a licensed corporation (Sch. 1, Pt 1). For a licensed corporation, a responsible officer is also its executive officer.
An individual licensed under s.120 to act for a licensed corporation in regulated activities. The individual is not a licensed corporation.
The statutory test under s.129 covering financial status, competence, conduct and reputation, applied to firms and to their officers.
Subsidiary legislation (Cap. 571N) setting the financial resources and paid-up share capital that licensed corporations must maintain.

title: Responsible officers, executive officers & MICs
oneLiner: Approved individuals carry personal accountability: responsible officers for licensed corporations, executive officers for banks, and managers-in-charge for senior management.
keyPoints: **Two layers:** The SFO sets the people regime for licensed corporations (LCs). For a bank registered to deal in securities, the Banking Ordinance adds an HKMA layer of [[executive officer]] approvals from the Monetary Authority (MA).

**Representatives and ROs:** An individual is licensed to act for an LC through accreditation. Only an approved [[responsible officer]] can supervise a regulated activity at the LC level, and each activity needs at least two.
**Managers-in-charge:** The SFC's MIC regime requires each LC to name an individual for each of eight [[core functions]], which reaches beyond the people who hold licences.
**Fitness and training:** Approval turns on fitness, sufficient authority and ongoing training. A lapse in any of these can cost an approval.
**Personal exposure:** Misconduct caused by the consent, connivance or neglect of a senior person can be treated as that person's own misconduct, and penalties can be imposed on individuals.
**Counsel's role:** Map every approval to a real role, track each one with an owner and a review date, and reconcile the SFC and HKMA lists.

conceptMap.caption: How the LC's approved people relate to the firm; a bank's executive officer layer sits on the same structure under the Banking Ordinance.
