deepDive.heading: The Part IV offer prohibition
deepDive.lede: Section 103 is the starting point for any offer or marketing communication aimed at the public.
points: **Scope:** s.103(1) makes it an offence to issue an advertisement, invitation or document that, to the issuer's knowledge, invites the public to enter into an agreement for securities or a structured product, or to take an interest in a [[collective investment scheme|Collective investment scheme]].
**Authorization route:** The offence does not apply where the SFC has authorized the issue under s.105(1).

**Exemptions:** s.103(2) lists exempt issuers and channels, including licensed intermediaries in certain product types, the Government, and communications to a company's own holders, creditors and employees. s.103(3) exempts a prospectus that complies with, or is exempt from, Part II of Cap. 32.

**Penalties:** On indictment the fine is $500,000 and imprisonment for 3 years, plus a daily fine for a continuing offence. On summary conviction the fine is at level 6 and imprisonment for 6 months (s.103(4)).

**Defence and carve-outs:** s.103(9) is a defence where the person took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence. s.103(5) and (6) add further carve-outs, so read them before relying on a private-audience argument.
deepDive.takeaway: Every app banner, product page and promotional message that invites a customer to invest is an advertisement for these purposes, so it needs an exemption or authorization before it goes live.

deepDive.heading: Product authorization under ss.104 and 105
deepDive.lede: The SFC authorizes funds and marketing material separately, and it can attach conditions to each.

visual.caption: Two authorizations with different subjects and the same approved-person condition.

items.label: s.104: the scheme
items.note: SFC may authorize a collective investment scheme, with conditions

items.label: s.105: the marketing
items.note: SFC may authorize an advertisement, invitation or document

items.label: Approved person
items.note: Each authorization needs an individual to receive SFC notices

points: **s.104:** The SFC may authorize a collective investment scheme on application, subject to conditions it considers appropriate. Under s.104(5) it may refuse where authorization is not in the interest of the investing public.
**s.105:** The SFC may separately authorize the issue of an advertisement, invitation or document that would otherwise fall within s.103(1), including conditions on the matter to which it relates.

**Approved person:** Both authorizations require an individual approved by the SFC to receive its notices. Changes to that person's contact details must be notified within 14 days (ss.104(2), 105(2)).

**Product codes:** The SFC Handbook for Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes and Unlisted Structured Investment Products sets the product criteria. Its Part I holds overarching principles that apply across its codes.
**Timing:** Build the authorization timetable into launch plans, because a campaign that goes live before authorization is an offence in itself.
deepDive.takeaway: Ask for the authorization scope early and confirm whether it covers the marketing material as well as the product, because that scope limits what the app can say.

deepDive.heading: Prospectuses under Cap. 32
deepDive.lede: Where no exemption applies, offers of shares and debentures follow the company-law prospectus rules.

visual.caption: The sequence for a share or debenture offer: a Seventeenth Schedule offer falls outside the prospectus rules, and otherwise a registered prospectus is needed.

items.label: Offer to the public
items.note: Invitation to take up shares or debentures

items.label: Seventeenth Schedule offer
items.note: Professional investors, up to 50 persons, or HK$500,000 and HK$5m limits

items.label: Registered prospectus
items.note: Content and language under s.38 and the Third Schedule

points: **s.38:** A prospectus must be in English with a Chinese translation, or in Chinese with an English translation, and must state the Third Schedule matters (s.38(1)). Non-compliance exposes the company and each knowing party to a fine (s.38(1B)).

**Application forms:** s.38(3) prohibits issuing an application form for shares or debentures unless it comes with a compliant prospectus, subject to exceptions, including offers not made to the public.

**Seventeenth Schedule:** Part 1 lists offers that fall outside the prospectus definition. These include offers to professional investors (para 1), offers to not more than 50 persons (para 2), offers with total consideration of at most $5,000,000 (para 3) and offers with a minimum denomination or consideration of at least $500,000 (para 4). Paras 2 to 4 also require the statement in Part 3 of the Eighteenth Schedule.
**Shareholder and group offers:** Paras 7 and 8 cover certain offers to existing holders and group members. Read their conditions before relying on them.
**Debentures and funds:** Debentures follow the same offer rules. Funds and structured products follow ss.103 to 105 instead, so a Cap. 32 analysis alone is not enough.
deepDive.takeaway: The Seventeenth Schedule tests are definition-driven, so record each limit (investor count, amounts and required statement) when the offer is designed rather than at launch.

deepDive.heading: Listing and the SFC copy
deepDive.lede: A listing application goes to the exchange and is copied to the SFC, which can ask questions and object.

visual.caption: Time limits run from the filing of the SFC copy, which is due within one business day after filing with the exchange.

items.label: Copy filed with SFC
items.note: After filing with the exchange (s.5(1))

items.label: SFC information request
items.note: Notice under s.6(1), from the date the copy is filed

items.label: Objection or no objection
items.note: From the copy filing, or from supply of further information (s.6(6))

points: **Two rulebooks:** The exchange's Listing Rules govern the listing itself. The Stock Market Listing Rules (Cap. 571V) set the SFC's parallel role.
**Dual filing:** The applicant files a copy of its application with the SFC within one business day after submitting it to the exchange (s.5(1)).
**Effect of objection:** An objection or a condition takes effect immediately (s.6(5)).
deepDive.takeaway: Diarise the SFC copy filing and the ten-business-day information window at the start of any listing timetable.

deepDive.heading: Funds and private vehicles
deepDive.lede: Fund structures have their own statutory routes, and a bank may take a role in them as distributor, depositary or custodian.
points: **Open-ended fund companies:** Part IVA of the SFO, starting at s.112A, creates a corporate form for open-ended fund companies. It covers registration, incorporation, share capital and sub-funds, directors and service providers, and the SFC's powers to give directions and cancel registration.

**Limited partnership funds:** The Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) has operated since 31 August 2020 and gives private funds a partnership vehicle. The fund has no separate legal personality and adds no new licence, so an investment manager still needs an SFC licence, for example Type 9 (asset management) for discretionary management from Hong Kong.

**Depositary roles:** A bank acting as depositary of a relevant CIS needs registration for Type 13 (providing depositary services for relevant CISs). Section 119 allows registration for any regulated activity except Type 3 and Type 8.

**Structure choice:** Private funds, authorized retail funds and open-ended fund companies bring different authorization, disclosure and tax consequences, so settle the structure before offer documents are prepared.
deepDive.takeaway: The fund vehicle determines which offer route applies, so settle it before any document is drafted.

deepDive.heading: Distribution by a bank
deepDive.lede: A bank that distributes products carries the product due diligence and conduct duties itself.
points: **Product due diligence:** Before offering a product, the bank should assess its structure, risks, costs and target investors, and record the review. The SFC Code of Conduct and SFC circulars set the expectations.
**Suitability and complex products:** Suitability and complex product rules apply to distribution and are covered in stage 5 of this module.
**Private banking:** An offer restricted to professional investors can rely on the Seventeenth Schedule (para 1), but the bank needs a documented client classification before each offer.

**Apps and social media:** Promotional content on apps and social media is an advertisement for s.103 purposes, even when the message is short, because the test is whether it invites the public to act.

**Placing and underwriting:** Bookbuilding and placing activities fall under paragraph 21 of the Code of Conduct, which took effect on 5 August 2022 and adds duties for the Overall Coordinator in share offerings.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat each channel, app message, social post and product page as an offer document, and clear it through the same authorization and exemption check.

provisions.title: Offence to issue advertisements, invitations or documents relating to investments in certain cases
provisions.summary: Makes it an offence to issue an advertisement, invitation or document that invites the public to deal in securities, a regulated investment agreement or other structured product, or a collective investment scheme, unless the SFC authorizes the issue under s.105(1) or an exemption applies. Exemptions are in s.103(2) and (3). The penalties are a $500,000 fine and 3 years' imprisonment on indictment, or a level 6 fine and 6 months on summary conviction, with daily fines for continuing offences (s.103(4)). Subsection (9) gives a due diligence defence.
provisions.counselNote: This is the core offence for any digital marketing that touches investment products. Each campaign needs a documented exemption or authorization reference before it goes live.

provisions.title: Commission may authorize collective investment schemes
provisions.summary: Allows the SFC to authorize a collective investment scheme on application, subject to conditions. Authorization requires an individual approved to receive SFC notices, and changes to that person's contact details must be notified within 14 days. The SFC may refuse where authorization is not in the interest of the investing public.
provisions.counselNote: Fund products offered to the public need this authorization. Confirm the approved person and the conditions attached before launch, and diarise contact-change notices.

provisions.title: Commission may authorize issue of advertisements, invitations or documents
provisions.summary: Allows the SFC to authorize the issue of an advertisement, invitation or document that would otherwise fall within s.103(1), subject to conditions that can cover the content and subject matter. Like s.104, it requires an approved person and contact-detail notifications.
provisions.counselNote: This is the route for marketing material for an authorized product. Conditions on content bind the app and web copy, so the marketing team needs them in writing.

provisions.title: Offence to fraudulently or recklessly induce others to invest money
provisions.summary: Makes it an offence to make a fraudulent or reckless misrepresentation to induce another person to acquire securities, a structured product or an interest in a collective investment scheme. On indictment the penalty is a fine of $1,000,000 and 7 years' imprisonment. On summary conviction it is a level 6 fine and 6 months' imprisonment.
provisions.counselNote: Marketing claims about returns, risk or product features must be accurate and supportable. Reckless statements in app copy can be criminal, not just a conduct issue.

provisions.title: Civil liability for inducing others to invest money in certain cases
provisions.summary: Makes a person who makes a fraudulent, reckless or negligent misrepresentation liable in damages for pecuniary loss that another person suffers by relying on it, where that person was induced to enter into one of the listed investment transactions. Liability applies whether or not any other liability also arises.
provisions.counselNote: The negligence limb reaches sales and marketing statements, not just deliberate misstatements. Review scripts and product summaries with that in mind.

provisions.instrument: Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32)
provisions.title: Specific requirements as to particulars in prospectus
provisions.summary: Requires a prospectus to be in English with a Chinese translation, or the reverse, and to state the matters in Part I of the Third Schedule. A non-compliant prospectus exposes the company and each knowing party to a fine. Application forms for shares or debentures may not be issued unless accompanied by a compliant prospectus, subject to exceptions.
provisions.counselNote: The application form is a common trap: a form issued in a digital journey without the prospectus breaches s.38(3) even if the offer is otherwise sound. Check the exceptions in the text before relying on them.

provisions.instrument: Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32)
provisions.title: Offers Specified for the Purposes of Paragraph (b)(ii) of the Definition of Prospectus in Section 2(1) of this Ordinance
provisions.summary: Lists offers that fall outside the prospectus definition: offers to professional investors, offers to not more than 50 persons, offers with total consideration of at most $5,000,000, and offers with a minimum denomination or consideration of at least $500,000. Paras 2 to 4 require the statement in Part 3 of the Eighteenth Schedule. Paras 7 and 8 cover certain offers to existing holders and group members.
provisions.counselNote: These limits are the usual route for private or pre-IPO placements by a bank. Record investor counts, amounts and the required statement for each offer, because the safe harbour is lost if a condition fails.

provisions.instrument: Securities and Futures (Stock Market Listing) Rules (Cap. 571V)
provisions.title: Powers of the Commission to require further information and to object to listing
provisions.summary: Allows the SFC, by notice given within 10 business days of the applicant filing its copy, to require further information. The SFC may object to a listing that does not comply with s.3, is false or misleading, or would not be in the interest of the investing public or the public interest. An objection takes effect immediately.
provisions.counselNote: The information request is the SFC's main tool in listing vetting. Build a response team and a timetable into the listing plan.

provisions.title: Open-ended Fund Companies
provisions.summary: Part IVA sets out the regime for open-ended fund companies, covering registration, incorporation, share capital and sub-funds, directors, service providers and the SFC's powers to give directions and cancel registration.
provisions.counselNote: An open-ended fund company is a corporate fund vehicle that the bank may need to distribute or service. Confirm the director duties and the regulatory approvals that apply before taking any role.

provisions.title: Limited partnership funds
provisions.summary: Provides a registration regime for limited partnership funds, a private fund vehicle that commenced operation on 31 August 2020. The fund has no separate legal personality and adds no new licence, so the investment manager remains subject to the SFC licensing regime.
provisions.counselNote: For a bank that services private funds, the question is the manager's licence and the bank's own role, not the Ordinance alone. Confirm both before a mandate is accepted.

provisions.instrument: SFC Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC
provisions.title: Bookbuilding and placing activities
provisions.summary: Sets conduct requirements for intermediaries carrying out bookbuilding and placing activities in equity and debt capital market transactions. The provision took effect on 5 August 2022 and sets further duties for the Overall Coordinator.
provisions.counselNote: A bank acting as an underwriter or placing agent must apply these rules to bookbuilding, including the Overall Coordinator's duties. Map the process and its records against the text.

provisions.instrument: SFC Handbook for Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, Investment-Linked Assurance Schemes and Unlisted Structured Investment Products
provisions.title: Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds
provisions.summary: Sets the SFC's product criteria for authorized unit trusts and mutual funds. Part I of the Handbook sets overarching principles that apply across the product codes, which also cover investment-linked assurance schemes and unlisted structured investment products.
provisions.counselNote: A bank selling authorized funds must match its distribution materials and processes to the Code and to the authorization conditions. Keep a record of the Code version each product was assessed against.

checklist: **Inventory offers:** List each product, channel and audience, and tag which route applies: authorization, prospectus or exemption.
**Clear marketing:** Route every advertisement, app message and social post through a documented s.103 check before publication.
**Track authorizations:** Keep a register of SFC authorizations, approved persons and conditions, and diarise the 14-day contact-change notices.
**Document exemptions:** Record the basis for each Seventeenth Schedule or s.103(2) exemption, with investor counts, amounts and required statements.
**Check the prospectus:** Confirm the Cap. 32 s.38 form, language and content before any application form is issued.
**Build a listing timetable:** Diarise the SFC copy filing and the ten-business-day information window in any listing plan.
**Map fund roles:** Confirm the bank's role in each fund (distributor, depositary or custodian) and the licence that role requires.
**Set product due diligence:** Adopt a board-approved review of products before the bank offers them, covering structure, risk, cost and target investors.
itAngle: **Campaign controls:** Digital marketing workflows need a publication gate that records the s.103 check, the exemption or authorization reference and the approver.
**Investor status data:** The professional investor and group offer tests depend on client data, so classification fields and their audit trail become part of the offer control.

**Document templates:** Prospectus and application form templates should pull the required Cap. 32 and Eighteenth Schedule statements from a controlled library, so a missing statement is caught before issue.
**Version control:** Keep offer material versioned, so the bank can show which version was authorized and when it was published.
bankNotes: **Authorized before distributed:** Public offers of funds and structured products need SFC authorization of the product and its offering documents, usually obtained by the issuer or manager. The bank must confirm it exists and use only authorized materials; its own promotional material needs an s.103(2) or (3) exemption or s.105 authorization.

**App marketing:** Banners, push notifications and product pages that invite a customer to invest are advertisements for s.103 purposes. Digital channels make them easy to publish without legal review.

**Private bank offers:** Offers only to professional investors can rely on the Seventeenth Schedule (para 1), but the bank needs a documented client classification before each offer, because a misclassification is an s.103 exposure.
**Registration scope:** Check that the bank's registration covers each regulated activity the offer involves, and that the product's authorization status is recorded before it goes on the platform.
pitfalls: **Launch before authorization:** Publishing a fund or structured product campaign before the s.104 or s.105 authorization is in place.
**Treating exemptions as automatic:** Assuming a professional investor or group offer falls outside s.103 without checking its conditions, including the Eighteenth Schedule statements.
**Forgetting the prospectus form rule:** Issuing an application form for shares or debentures without the prospectus it must accompany (s.38(3)).
**Outdated rule texts:** Citing an earlier version of Cap. 571V or the Code without confirming the amendments in force for the offer.

glossary.definition: An arrangement in which investors pool money or assets to share in profits or income from a portfolio managed by others. Offers of interests to the public in Hong Kong need s.104 authorization or an exemption.
A product whose return is linked to underlying assets, indices or other reference points. Section 103(1)(a)(ii) brings it within the offer prohibition alongside regulated investment agreements.
A document offering shares or debentures to the public. Under Cap. 32 s.38 it must meet the content and language rules unless an exemption applies.
An investor type defined in Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the SFO. Paragraph 1 of Part 1 of the Seventeenth Schedule relies on it for offers that need no prospectus.
An offer listed in Part 1 of the Seventeenth Schedule to Cap. 32 that falls outside the prospectus definition, such as an offer to not more than 50 persons that carries the required statement.

Collecting investor orders or indications of interest to set the price and allocation of a securities offering. Paragraph 21 of the Code of Conduct regulates intermediaries in bookbuilding and placing.
A corporate fund vehicle under Part IVA of the SFO whose shares can be redeemed. It lets an investment fund take the form of a company.
A private fund structure under Cap. 637 that is registered as a limited partnership. It adds no separate licence for the manager, which still needs an SFC licence.

title: Online platforms, technology & virtual assets
oneLiner: Trading apps, cloud records and virtual assets each attract SFC technology rules, and counsel can map them before the SFC does.
keyPoints: **Electronic trading:** Paragraph 18 of the Code of Conduct and Schedule 7 set the standards for trading systems, including [[direct market access]] and algorithmic services.
**Cyber security:** The SFC's 2017 anti-hacking guidelines made [[two-factor authentication]] for client logins a baseline control for internet trading.
**Records:** Section 130 of the SFO and the SFC's 2019 circular on external storage govern where regulatory records may be kept, including with a cloud provider.
**Online platforms:** The 2019 Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms apply suitability and disclosure standards to digital journeys and [[robo-advice]].

**Virtual assets:** Trading platforms need a licence under Part 5B of the AMLO, and intermediaries follow the HKMA and SFC joint circular of 22 December 2023 while the dealing and custody regime is still at the proposal stage.
**Counsel's role:** Map each customer journey, system and record store against these rules before launch, and keep that map current.

deepDive.heading: Electronic trading and algorithmic systems
deepDive.lede: Paragraph 18 of the Code of Conduct sets the baseline for any electronic trading system a licensed or registered person uses.
points: **Scope:** Paragraph 18 covers electronic trading, including internet trading. Schedule 7 adds requirements for [[direct market access]] and algorithmic trading providers.
**System adequacy:** The system must be reliable, secure and of adequate capacity, with contingency arrangements in place.
**Testing and change:** Schedule 7 expects trading systems to be tested and reviewed regularly, and again when they are modified.
**Erroneous orders:** Algorithmic controls must prevent erroneous order instructions from reaching the market.
**Supervision and records:** Supervision of the system and record keeping are part of the compliance evidence the SFC will ask for.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat each trading channel as a regulated system, with a named owner, test evidence on file and a tested contingency plan.

deepDive.heading: Cyber security for internet trading
deepDive.lede: The 2017 anti-hacking guidelines set the SFC's baseline for client-facing trading channels.

visual.caption: Three controls to evidence for a client-facing trading app.

items.label: Client login
items.note: Two-factor authentication applies from this date

items.label: Wider baseline
items.note: Other baseline requirements apply from this date

items.label: Documented risk assessment
items.note: Authentication proportionate to the business model

points: **Two-factor authentication:** Required for client logins to internet trading accounts, using any two of: something the client knows, has or is.
**Scope:** The guidelines apply to licensed and registered persons that carry on internet trading.
**Proportionality:** The authentication solution must suit the firm's business model, so the choice of factors should be documented and justified.
**Parallel HKMA circular:** The HKMA issued a parallel circular asking registered institutions to tighten their internet trading security in line with the SFC guidelines.
deepDive.takeaway: Keep the authentication design, its risk assessment and its go-live dates in the compliance file, not only in IT documentation.

deepDive.heading: Records, cloud storage and messaging
deepDive.lede: Records must be kept, retrievable and open to SFC inspection, wherever the bank keeps them.
points: **Premises approval:** Under s.130(3) a licensed corporation needs the SFC's prior written approval before using any premises to keep records. The SFC may approve premises under s.130(1).

**External storage:** The SFC's circular of 31 October 2019 sets conditions for keeping regulatory records only with an [[external electronic data storage]] provider, with no duplicate on the firm's premises. The firm must notify the SFC, name two Managers-In-Charge and confirm that records are accessible on demand at its principal place of business.
**Risk expectations:** Outsourcing storage does not outsource responsibility. Cyber and operational risks stay with the firm, whichever storage model it uses.
**Data centres:** Where an external provider holds records and no contemporaneous copy is kept at approved premises, the provider's data centre counts as the premises for section 130 purposes.
**Chats are records:** Staff messages used for client business need the same retention and retrieval controls as email and voice.
deepDive.takeaway: Decide where each category of regulatory record lives, who can retrieve it and how it would reach the SFC on request.

deepDive.heading: Online platforms and robo-advice
deepDive.lede: The online platform guidelines apply the same suitability and disclosure standards to digital journeys.

visual.caption: The guidelines cover two kinds of digital service.

items.label: Online distribution
items.note: Platform design, suitability and disclosure apply as they do offline

items.label: Robo-advice
items.note: Automated advice has its own chapter in the guidelines

points: **Scope:** The Guidelines took effect on 6 July 2019 and apply to licensed and registered persons that execute orders, distribute or advise on investment products through online platforms.

**Six core principles:** CP1 to CP6 cover platform design, information for clients, platform operations and technology risk management, governance capabilities and resources, review and monitoring, and record keeping.
**Complex products:** Complex products offered on a platform attract extra protections, including suitability checks and prominent warnings.
**Remote onboarding:** The SFC publishes acceptable approaches for client identity verification and account opening, and a bank follows the HKMA's remote onboarding expectations.
deepDive.takeaway: Map each platform journey against the six principles before go-live, and keep the mapping in the compliance file.

deepDive.heading: Virtual assets: licensing and tokenisation
deepDive.lede: Virtual asset activity has its own licences, and the rules for intermediaries are still being built out.

points: **Trading platforms:** Providing virtual asset services in Hong Kong as a business requires a licence under Part 5B of the AMLO (s.53ZRD).

**Intermediaries:** The HKMA and SFC joint circular of 22 December 2023, supplemented on 30 September 2025 to allow staking on conditions, sets terms for intermediaries' virtual asset activities. Only Type 1 licensees or registrants may offer dealing, and then only through or with an SFC-licensed platform, for example via an [[omnibus account]].

**Tokenisation:** The SFC circular of 2 November 2023 on intermediaries' [[tokenised securities]] activities still applies. On 20 April 2026 the SFC updated its 2 November 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorised products and issued a circular on secondary trading of tokenised products on licensed VA trading platforms.
**Stablecoins:** Stablecoin issuers are licensed by the HKMA under the Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656), in force since 1 August 2025, a separate regime to cross-refer to the digital assets stage.

**Proposed:** Consultation conclusions published on 24 December 2025 propose new AMLO licensing regimes for VA dealing and VA custody. The authorities said they would introduce an amending bill in 2026, so check whether it has been introduced or passed.
deepDive.takeaway: Decide, activity by activity, which licence applies today, and treat the dealing and custody regime as a pending obligation, not a current one.

deepDive.heading: The bank's technology stack under the SFO
deepDive.lede: Outsourcing, change control and incident handling link the bank's technology to its SFC and HKMA obligations.
points: **Outsourcing:** A vendor running a regulated function does not move the responsibility. Contract terms must give the bank audit rights and give the SFC access to records.
**Change management:** Changes to trading, records or onboarding systems should be tested and approved, with an audit trail the SFC can inspect.
**Incident reporting:** System failures and hacking incidents need prompt notice to the SFC or HKMA, so the incident plan should name who decides and how fast.
**Operational resilience:** HKMA resilience expectations run alongside the SFC controls, so one incident plan should serve both regulators.
deepDive.takeaway: Keep one incident and change register that answers to both the SFC and the HKMA.

provisions.instrument: Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission
provisions.title: Electronic trading and algorithmic trading requirements
provisions.summary: Paragraph 18 covers electronic trading. It makes a licensed or registered person responsible for orders sent through its systems and requires reliable, secure and adequate-capacity systems, risk management controls (including over algorithmic orders), testing and record keeping. Schedule 7 sets additional requirements for internet trading, direct market access and algorithmic trading. Paragraph 18 and Schedule 7 came into force on 1 January 2014.
provisions.counselNote: A trading app or API route that takes client orders is an electronic trading system for this purpose. Map its controls to para 18 and Sch. 7 before launch, and keep the test and change evidence.

provisions.title: Regulated activities: Type 7, providing automated trading services
provisions.summary: Schedule 5 lists Type 7, providing automated trading services, among the regulated activities for which a licence is required.
provisions.counselNote: If the bank runs an automated order-routing service for clients, check whether it carries on Type 7 and how that sits alongside its registration as an RI.

provisions.title: Suitability of premises for keeping records or documents
provisions.summary: The SFC may approve premises for a licensed corporation to keep records required under the SFO or the AMLO, and the SFC must be satisfied the premises are suitable. A licensed corporation must not, without the SFC's prior written approval, use any premises for keeping records relating to the regulated activity for which it is licensed.
provisions.counselNote: This is the SFC's control over where records sit. Before adopting a new storage location, check whether it is premises for this section and whether the RI registration engages it.

provisions.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615)
provisions.title: Licence required for carrying on VA service business
provisions.summary: Part 5B regulates virtual asset services. Section 53ZRD requires a licence to carry on a VA service business, and Part 5B governs the licensing of virtual asset trading platforms.
provisions.counselNote: A digital bank offering virtual asset trading to Hong Kong customers needs a licence under this Part, separate from any SFO registration. Decide the licensing route before launch.

provisions.instrument: SFC Guidelines for Reducing and Mitigating Hacking Risks Associated with Internet Trading
provisions.title: Anti-hacking guidelines for internet trading
provisions.summary: Issued on 27 October 2017 together with a parallel HKMA circular to registered institutions. Two-factor authentication for client logins applied from 27 April 2018, and the other requirements from 27 July 2018.
provisions.counselNote: The guidelines set the SFC's baseline for any app or web trading channel. Keep the authentication design, its risk assessment and its go-live dates on file, and read the HKMA's parallel circular with the SFC text.

provisions.instrument: SFC circular: licensed corporations' use of external electronic data storage
provisions.title: External electronic data storage for regulatory records
provisions.summary: Explains how licensed corporations may keep regulatory records with an external electronic data storage provider. Where records are kept only with the provider, the firm must notify the SFC and name two Managers-In-Charge who can produce them, and records must be accessible on demand at its principal place of business. A data centre used by the provider can count as premises for section 130.
provisions.counselNote: This is the main route for cloud record keeping. For a bank, the HKMA's outsourcing and cloud expectations apply alongside this circular, so map the storage design against both.

provisions.instrument: SFC Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms
provisions.title: Online distribution and advisory platforms
provisions.summary: Effective 6 July 2019. Sets six core principles for designing and operating online platforms and for applying suitability online, with a chapter on robo-advice.
provisions.counselNote: The bank's onboarding, product selection and advice journeys are the platforms this guidance describes. Map each journey to the six principles and record the design choices.

provisions.ref: Code of Conduct para 5.1 and approaches page
provisions.title: Acceptable account opening approaches
provisions.summary: The SFC publishes acceptable approaches for client identity verification and account opening, including remote onboarding of overseas individual clients from eligible jurisdictions.
provisions.counselNote: Remote onboarding is the most likely route to new securities clients. Check the approaches page and the eligible jurisdictions list before any change to the onboarding flow.

provisions.instrument: HKMA and SFC joint circular on intermediaries' virtual asset-related activities
provisions.ref: Joint circular, 22 December 2023; supplemental joint circular, 30 September 2025
provisions.title: Intermediaries' virtual asset-related activities
provisions.summary: Sets conditions for intermediaries' virtual asset-related activities, including dealing and advising. Only firms licensed or registered for Type 1 may offer virtual asset dealing, and omnibus account arrangements with an SFC-licensed platform must follow prescribed terms. It superseded the joint circulars of 20 October 2023 and 28 January 2022, and a supplemental joint circular of 30 September 2025 allows intermediaries to offer staking on conditions.
provisions.counselNote: A registered institution that wants to offer virtual asset dealing through an omnibus account with a platform must follow the prescribed terms in the circular's appendices, and check the terms of the current version before launch.

provisions.instrument: SFC circulars: tokenisation of SFC-authorised products and intermediaries' tokenised securities activities
provisions.title: Tokenised securities
provisions.summary: The 2 November 2023 intermediaries circular on tokenised securities-related activities still applies. The 2023 circular on tokenising SFC-authorised products, which supported tokenised funds and structured products for primary dealing, was updated on 20 April 2026. A circular of the same date sets a framework for secondary trading of tokenised products on licensed VA trading platforms.
provisions.counselNote: Tokenised products need the same ownership and record controls as conventional products, whoever runs the ledger.

provisions.instrument: SFC: ASPIRe roadmap for virtual assets
provisions.title: ASPIRe roadmap
provisions.summary: A policy roadmap with twelve initiatives under five pillars: Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships. Its initiatives include new frameworks for OTC trading and custodial services and optimised operational requirements for trading platforms. The SFC describes it as a living blueprint.
provisions.counselNote: The roadmap shows the direction of travel for licensing and products. Treat each initiative as a proposal until a circular or rule implements it.

provisions.title: Offence related to carrying on regulated stablecoin activity
provisions.summary: Section 8 prohibits carrying on a regulated stablecoin activity, or holding oneself out as doing so, unless the person is licensed or exempted. Licences are granted under section 15. Contravention is an offence with fines and imprisonment on conviction.
provisions.counselNote: Stablecoin activity sits in the HKMA regime, not the SFC regime. Cross-refer to the digital assets stage when a client product references a stablecoin.

checklist: **Inventory trading channels:** List every app, web, API and messaging route that takes client orders, and bring each within para 18 and Schedule 7.
**Document authentication:** Record the two-factor design for client logins, its risk assessment and its go-live date against the anti-hacking guidelines.
**Map record stores:** For each category of regulatory record, name the location, provider, premises status and retrieval route.
**Test trading systems:** Keep test plans, change approvals and capacity results on file, and confirm that contingency arrangements work.
**Review platform journeys:** Map onboarding, product selection and advice flows to the six online platform principles before any launch.
**Confirm the VA licensing route:** Decide, per activity, whether Part 5B of the AMLO, the SFO or the joint circular applies, and whether an [[omnibus account]] is needed.
**Track pending VA rules:** Diary the VA dealing and custody proposals and the ASPIRe initiatives, with an owner for each.
**Agree incident triggers:** Set reporting triggers for hacking incidents and system failures that reach both the SFC and the HKMA, with decision owners and timelines.
itAngle: **Control mapping:** Keep one control register linking each SFC requirement to the system, owner and test evidence that satisfies it.
**Logs as evidence:** Order logs, change tickets and access records are regulatory evidence, so keep them in a form the SFC can read on request.
**API channels:** An API that lets third-party apps send orders is a trading channel, so the same controls and records requirements apply to it.
**Cloud contracts:** Storage and processing contracts should set SFC access, audit rights and exit steps, so that the 2019 circular conditions can be met.
bankNotes: **Dual route:** An RI operates under its SFO registration and the HKMA's supervisory framework, so HKMA technology risk and operational resilience expectations apply alongside the SFC controls.
**Parallel circular:** The HKMA asked registered institutions to strengthen internet trading security in line with the SFC guidelines, so check the HKMA circular as well as the SFC text.
**Joint circular for banks:** Only a Type 1 registrant may offer virtual asset dealing, and an [[omnibus account]] runs through an SFC-licensed platform. The bank's own terms sit on top of that.
**Digital onboarding:** Remote account opening for securities clients sits alongside the bank's banking onboarding rules. Align the two so one identity check serves both where the rules allow.
pitfalls: **Treating the app as IT:** Assuming a trading app sits outside the Code of Conduct because it is a technology product rather than a channel for regulated activity.
**Late cloud move:** Moving regulatory records to a new provider without checking premises approval or whether an on-premises duplicate is needed.
**Stale circulars:** Relying on the 2023 joint and tokenisation circulars without checking the 20 April 2026 circulars on tokenised products and secondary trading.
**Building on proposals:** Building a [[robo-advice]] or dealing feature on proposed virtual asset rules before the bill is enacted and its terms are known.

glossary.definition: An authorized institution, such as a licensed bank, that is registered by the SFC to carry on one or more regulated activities.
Services that provide an automated system for trading, typically through algorithms or order routing. Type 7 in Schedule 5 to the SFO.
A service that lets clients send orders to a market through the intermediary's systems, subject to the controls in Schedule 7 to the Code of Conduct.
Login security that uses two of three factors: something the client knows, something the client has, or who the client is.
Keeping regulatory records with an outside provider, permitted under the SFC circular of 31 October 2019 subject to conditions.
An account held in an intermediary's name for several clients together. Here it routes virtual asset dealing through an SFC-licensed platform.
Automated, algorithm-based investment advice given through an online platform. It has its own chapter in the online platform guidelines.
Securities or fund interests represented as tokens on a ledger, with ownership recorded in the token system.

title: Market misconduct & insider dealing
oneLiner: The same six forms of misconduct can be pursued civilly or criminally, so information controls inside the bank are the first line of defence.
keyPoints: **Two routes:** Part XIII (civil, before the [[Market Misconduct Tribunal]]) and Part XIV (criminal) cover the same six forms of [[market misconduct]].
**Insider dealing:** A connected person who knows [[inside information]] and deals on it, or counsels or procures another to deal, commits market misconduct and an offence.
**Manipulation:** False trading, price rigging and stock market manipulation distort the market itself; the two disclosure forms distort the information the market relies on.
**Sanctions:** The Tribunal can impose director bans, cease-and-desist orders, disgorgement and costs; on indictment, criminal courts can impose a HK$10 million fine and 10 years' imprisonment.

**Listed corporations:** Part XIVA requires prompt public disclosure of inside information, subject to exceptions, and places duties on officers, backed by a regulatory fine of up to HK$8 million in some cases.
**Bank exposure:** Lending, underwriting and research give a bank access to inside information, so information barriers, restricted lists and staff dealing controls are compliance essentials.
