deepDive.heading: Complaints handling
deepDive.lede: A complaint is the first step, and the firm controls how it is handled.
points: **Duty:** The SFC Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC (Code of Conduct) para 12.3 requires complaints to be handled in a timely and appropriate way.

**FDRC notice:** If internal handling does not resolve the complaint, the firm must tell the client about the right to refer it to the Financial Dispute Resolution Centre (Code of Conduct para 12.3(c), as amended in 2012).
**Wider issues:** A complaint that may reveal problems affecting other clients should be investigated even where those clients have not complained (para 12.3(d)).
**Participation:** Licensed and registered persons must comply with the FDRS and be bound by the outcome of its dispute resolution process (para 12A, introduced in 2012).
**Records:** Keep complaint logs with root-cause analysis and remediation, because inspections look at how complaints were handled, not only at the outcome.
deepDive.takeaway: Make the FDRC notice part of every final reply, and treat each complaint as a potential regulatory event.

deepDive.heading: Financial Dispute Resolution Scheme
deepDive.lede: The FDRS is the low-cost route for monetary disputes with member institutions.

items.label: Complaint to the firm
items.note: Written complaint and a final written reply

items.label: FDRC mediation
items.note: Default route; standard claims up to HK$1 million

items.label: Arbitration
items.note: Used if mediation does not resolve the dispute

points: **Scheme:** The [[FDRC|Financial Dispute Resolution Centre]] runs the Financial Dispute Resolution Scheme (FDRS), which uses mediation first and arbitration next.
**Membership:** Institutions authorized by the HKMA or licensed or registered with the SFC must join, so a bank that is also an RI is a member.
**Claim limit:** Since 2018 the standard limit has been HK$1 million; larger claims can be handled with the parties' consent.
**Eligibility:** Claimants are generally individuals or small enterprises who have first made a written complaint and received a final written reply.
**Terms of Reference:** Eligibility and procedure are set by the FDRC's Terms of Reference.
deepDive.takeaway: The final-reply trigger and the claim limit decide whether the FDRC is available, so draft complaint replies with both in mind.

deepDive.heading: Investor Compensation Fund
deepDive.lede: The ICF compensates clients of an intermediary that defaults, within rules and limits.

items.label: Default by a specified person
items.note: Or an associated person, in connection with specified products

items.label: Payment from the fund
items.note: Capped per investor under the Compensation Limits Rules

points: **Purpose:** Section 236(1) requires the SFC to establish and maintain the Investor Compensation Fund to compensate clients who lose money because of a default by a specified person or an associated person.

**Who is covered:** A specified person includes an intermediary licensed or registered for Type 1 or Type 2 regulated activity, and an intermediary licensed for Type 8 (s.236(2)). A registered institution in those activities is therefore within scope.
**Products:** Covered products are securities or futures contracts listed or traded on a recognized stock or futures market, or on markets prescribed under s.244 (s.236(2)).

**Funding and priority:** The fund is built from claim-related payments, borrowings and reserves (s.237(1), (2)). Payments out of the fund, covering expenses and claims alike, are made as required and in an order the SFC determines (s.242(1)).

**Limit:** The Chief Executive in Council sets the maximum compensation per claimant (s.244(1)(b)). The Securities and Futures (Investor Compensation—Compensation Limits) Rules (Cap. 571AC) set HK$500,000 per investor per default for defaults on or after 1 January 2020, applied separately to securities and to futures contracts.
deepDive.takeaway: The ICF is a backstop with a cap, not full recovery; the default date and product scope decide the claim.

deepDive.heading: Civil claims against the firm
deepDive.lede: Clients can also sue, and the statute sets the tests for liability.
points: **s.108:** A person who makes a fraudulent, reckless or negligent misrepresentation that induces another to invest is liable in damages for the loss that reliance on it caused (s.108(1)).
**Directors:** Where a company made the misrepresentation, a director at the time is presumed to have made it unless he proves he did not authorize it (s.108(2)).

**ss.281 and 305:** Liability for market misconduct (s.281) and for contravening the relevant Divisions (s.305) requires that it be fair, just and reasonable in the circumstances (s.281(2), s.305(2)).
**Codes:** A failure to comply with a code does not by itself give rise to proceedings, but the code is admissible and is taken into account (s.399(6)).

**Non-reliance terms:** A clause stating that the client did not rely on representations outside the contract may be tested for fairness under the unconscionability and exemption-clause legislation, so the sales record must match what the clause says.
deepDive.takeaway: Claims turn on what was represented, to whom and whether reliance was reasonable, so the sales record matters as much as the product terms.

deepDive.heading: When an intermediary fails
deepDive.lede: The route depends on the type of firm: an SFC-licensed corporation, an RI or a bank.
points: **Restriction and discipline:** Section 204 lets the SFC restrict a licensed corporation's business by notice; for a registered institution, s.196 allows the SFC to revoke or suspend its registration.
**Winding up:** The SFC may petition to wind up a corporation in the public interest (s.212(1)), but an authorized financial institution is excluded from that power.

**Bank resolution:** For a bank, the Financial Institutions (Resolution) Ordinance (Cap. 628) applies. The Monetary Authority is the resolution authority for banking sector entities such as authorized institutions (s.2, definition of resolution authority), and Part 2 sets out the resolution authorities and their powers.

**Client assets:** Segregated client money and securities held under the client asset rules are held on trust for clients and are not available to the firm's creditors; recovery depends on the records and reconciliations.
deepDive.takeaway: Know which regime applies before a failure: SFO tools for securities business, and the banking resolution regime for the bank itself.

deepDive.heading: Lessons from Lehman-linked Minibonds
deepDive.lede: The 2008 Minibonds episode shaped how product sales and complaints are supervised.
points: **Background:** Minibonds linked to Lehman Brothers were sold to retail clients through distributing banks, and many lost heavily when Lehman collapsed in 2008.

**2009 scheme:** On 22 July 2009 the SFC, the HKMA and 16 distributing banks agreed, without admission of liability, to repurchase eligible Minibonds at 60% of the original investment's nominal value for customers under 65 and 70% for those 65 and over.
**Trade-off:** The SFC dropped its investigations into the banks' sales, and the HKMA said it would not pursue enforcement against banks in cases where customers accepted the offer.

**Lesson:** The episode was followed by investor-protection measures for bank sales, including audio recording of sales conversations, segregation of deposit and investment business and risk profiling of clients, and was followed in 2012 by the establishment of the FDRC.
deepDive.takeaway: Complex product sales are where complaints and claims cluster, so suitability and disclosure records must be strong from the start.

provisions.instrument: SFC Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC
provisions.title: Complaints handling and participation in the FDRS
provisions.summary: Requires licensed and registered persons to handle complaints appropriately and to tell clients about their right to refer an unresolved complaint to the FDRC. A complaint that may reveal wider issues must be investigated. A 2012 amendment added a duty to take part in the FDRS process (para 12A).
provisions.counselNote: Use para 12.3 as the basis for the complaint procedure and the FDRC notice. Quote the Code's current wording from the SFC's published version when briefing the board.

provisions.instrument: Financial Dispute Resolution Scheme (FDRS) and FDRC Terms of Reference
provisions.title: Financial Dispute Resolution Scheme
provisions.summary: Provides mediation, then arbitration, for monetary disputes between consumers and member institutions. Institutions authorized by the HKMA or licensed or registered with the SFC must join. The standard claim limit is HK$1 million, and larger claims need the parties' consent. Eligibility is set by the Terms of Reference.
provisions.counselNote: Route complaints so that the final-reply and eligibility conditions are met. Confirm the current claim limit and Terms of Reference before advising a client.

provisions.title: Establishment of compensation fund
provisions.summary: Requires the SFC to establish and maintain the Investor Compensation Fund, to compensate clients of a specified person who lose money through a default by that person or an associated person in connection with specified securities or futures contracts. Specified persons include intermediaries registered for Type 1 or Type 2 regulated activity and those licensed for Type 8.
provisions.counselNote: A registered institution doing dealing or advising work is within scope, so its securities defaults and those of its employees and client-asset holders can give rise to claims. Map which activities of the bank fall within Type 1, 2 or 8.

provisions.title: Rules by Chief Executive in Council and Commission
provisions.summary: Lets the Chief Executive in Council make rules on funding the compensation fund and on the maximum compensation a claimant may receive (s.244(1)). The SFC may make claims rules, after consulting the Financial Secretary on some matters (s.244(2), (3)). Funding rules must, so far as reasonably practicable, place the cost on market participants (s.244(4)).
provisions.counselNote: The limits and claims mechanics sit in subsidiary rules, not the Ordinance itself. Compliance should track the rules as amended and record the version it relies on.

provisions.instrument: Securities and Futures (Investor Compensation-Compensation Limits) Rules (Cap. 571AC)
provisions.title: Investor compensation limit
provisions.summary: The Securities and Futures (Investor Compensation-Compensation Limits) Rules set the maximum at HK$500,000 per investor per default for defaults on or after 1 January 2020. The limit was raised from HK$150,000 by L.N. 132 of 2019 and applies separately to securities and to futures contracts.
provisions.counselNote: Record HK$500,000 per investor per default and the default date in every ICF analysis, because the default date decides which limit applies.

provisions.title: Civil liability for inducing others to invest money in certain cases
provisions.summary: Makes a person who makes a fraudulent, reckless or negligent misrepresentation that induces another to enter an investment agreement, structured product or collective investment scheme liable in damages for the loss from relying on it. A director at the time of a company's misrepresentation is presumed to have made it unless he proves otherwise. A claim may be brought without a criminal charge or conviction.
provisions.counselNote: Misrepresentations in marketing or sales materials are the main exposure. Keep the approved materials and the record of what was said to each client.

provisions.title: Civil liability for market misconduct
provisions.summary: Makes a person who commits market misconduct (s.281) or contravenes the relevant Divisions of the Part (s.305) liable in damages for pecuniary loss resulting from it. In each case liability arises only if it is fair, just and reasonable in the circumstances. A determination by the Market Misconduct Tribunal can be admissible in such an action.
provisions.counselNote: A claim can be brought without any prosecution. Map market-misconduct and disclosure risks in the bank's securities activities as potential civil exposure, not only regulatory exposure.

provisions.title: Codes or guidelines by Commission
provisions.summary: Provides that failing to comply with a code or guideline does not by itself make a person liable to proceedings. The code is admissible in any proceedings under the Ordinance, and a relevant provision is taken into account in deciding the question before the court.
provisions.counselNote: The Code of Conduct informs a court's view of the standard of conduct without itself giving a cause of action. Its breaches still matter for SFC supervision.

provisions.title: Winding-up orders and bankruptcy orders
provisions.summary: Allows the SFC to petition to wind up a corporation of a class the court may wind up, where that is desirable in the public interest, on a just-and-equitable basis. The power does not extend to an authorized financial institution. Separate provision covers bankruptcy petitions against licensed representatives.
provisions.counselNote: For a bank, a failure would be handled by the HKMA and the resolution regime rather than an SFC petition. Set out the division of responsibility in the bank's failure playbook.

provisions.title: Disciplinary action in respect of registered institutions, etc.
provisions.summary: Section 196 lets the SFC discipline a regulated person found guilty of misconduct or not fit and proper, including for a registered institution by revoking or suspending its registration. Section 204 lets the SFC restrict a licensed corporation's business by notice, including by prohibiting certain transactions or solicitations.
provisions.counselNote: For a bank that is an RI, the registration-based powers in s.196 apply, while s.204 restricts a licensed corporation. Confirm which applies to the bank's entity and activity.

provisions.title: Deposits Specified for Purposes of Definitions of Protected Deposit and Relevant Deposit in Section 2(1) of this Ordinance
provisions.summary: Excludes from protected deposits, among others, term deposits whose current term exceeds five years (para 1(a)), structured deposits (para 1(aa)) and deposits taken at offices outside Hong Kong (para 1(d)). The protected deposit definition in s.2(1) incorporates these exclusions.
provisions.counselNote: Structured deposits sold by the bank are outside deposit protection, so customer materials must not imply otherwise. Mark this exclusion in the product disclosures for structured deposits.

provisions.title: Resolution Authorities
provisions.summary: Part 2 sets out the resolution authorities and their general powers, including the resolution objectives (s.8) and the general power of the resolution authority (s.11). Under the s.2 definition, the Monetary Authority is the resolution authority for banking sector entities such as authorized institutions.
provisions.counselNote: A bank's failure runs through the resolution regime, not the SFO. Set out the Monetary Authority's powers under Cap. 628 in the failure playbook.

checklist: **Map complaint routing:** Trace each complaint from the front line to the firm's process and to the FDRC notice, and record each step.
**Put the FDRC notice in every final reply**, and confirm eligibility under the FDRS Terms of Reference before drafting.
**Track ICF coverage by product:** Confirm whether each product is a specified securities or futures contract on a recognized market, and record the default date.
**Record the compensation limit:** Record HK$500,000 per investor per default and the default date in each ICF analysis.
**Review civil exposure** for misrepresentation (s.108) and market misconduct (ss.281, 305) in product disclosure and marketing.
**Prepare a failure playbook** covering SFC powers (ss.196, 204), the winding-up limit (s.212), bank resolution (Cap. 628) and client-asset recovery.
**Separate structured deposits from deposit protection** in all customer communications (Cap. 581, Sch. 1, para 1(aa)).
**Keep complaint and remediation records** ready for SFC and HKMA review, with root-cause analysis for each.
itAngle: **Complaint data:** Complaint logs are regulatory records. Capture the channel, product, timestamps and root-cause tags so that the FDRC notice and the complaint history can be produced quickly.
**Digital-channel evidence:** For online sales and complaints, keep the disclosures shown, their versions and the time of each customer acceptance, because these are the evidence in a s.108 dispute.
**Automated replies:** Chatbot or templated complaint responses must still meet the final-reply and FDRC-notice requirements, so the system needs a route to a human.
**Trade and order records:** ICF and FDRS claims depend on reliable records of trades and client instructions, so retention and retrieval of those records are compliance controls.
bankNotes: **FDRS membership:** A bank authorized by the HKMA that is also an RI must join the FDRS, so its complaint replies must carry the FDRC notice.
**ICF scope:** A bank registered for Type 1 or Type 2 is a specified person under s.236(2), so claims can arise from defaults of the bank or its associated persons in exchange-traded products.
**Deposit protection:** Structured deposits are excluded from protected deposits (Cap. 581, Sch. 1, para 1(aa)), and deposits taken at offices outside Hong Kong are also excluded (para 1(d)).

**Cross-border clients:** Clients served from outside Hong Kong raise separate questions: FDRS eligibility depends on the service being provided in Hong Kong, and deposits taken at offices outside Hong Kong are not protected (Cap. 581, Sch. 1, para 1(d)).
pitfalls: **Silent final reply:** Closing a complaint without stating the right to refer it to the FDRC, which can delay or defeat the FDRS route.
**Discounting the Code:** Treating a Code breach as having no consequence. The Code is admissible in court and taken into account (s.399(6)).
**Overstating the ICF:** Assuming that every product or intermediary is covered. Coverage is limited to specified securities or futures contracts on recognized markets (s.236).
**Implying deposit protection:** Describing structured deposits as protected in customer materials.
